response.description: Treatment-blind gradient-boosted classifier ranking users by predicted conversion probability P(Y=1|X). The conventional targeting policy: it identifies who will convert, not who converts because of the ad.

constant.description: Applies the sample average treatment effect to every user. Equivalent to random targeting and to assuming the effect is homogeneous; it is the floor that any heterogeneous-effect model must beat.

s_learner.description: Single gradient-boosted classifier with the treatment indicator appended as one more feature; uplift is f(x,1) - f(x,0). Shares statistical strength across arms but is biased toward zero effect, because the learner rarely splits on one weak binary feature among many stronger ones.

t_learner.description: Two independent gradient-boosted classifiers, one per treatment arm; uplift is mu_1(x) - mu_0(x). Captures heterogeneity without shrinking it, at the cost of a much noisier control-arm model under this dataset's 85/15 split.

x_learner.description: X-learner (Künzel et al. 2019): imputes individual effects on observed units, regresses them on X within each arm, then blends by the propensity score so the arm with more data dominates. Designed for exactly the lopsided 85/15 allocation in this dataset.

dr_learner.description: Cross-fitted doubly-robust learner: builds AIPW pseudo-outcomes with out-of-fold nuisance predictions and regresses them on X with an L1 objective. Consistent if either the outcome or the propensity model is correct; the reference estimator here.
